title: Half-circle displacement
subject: Physics
stem: A particle travels from one end of a diameter to the opposite end along a semicircular path of radius r. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
raw_stem: A particle travels from one end of a diameter to the opposite end along a semicircular path of radius r. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
correct: The displacement magnitude is 2r, the straight-line diameter joining the endpoints. The semicircle arc length is distance travelled, not displacement.
steps: The displacement magnitude is 2r, the straight-line diameter joining the endpoints. The semicircle arc length is distance travelled, not displacement.
trap: Do not confuse the curved semicircular path length (distance) with the straight-line displacement between diameter endpoints.
teacher_check: Straight-line chord joining endpoints across a circle diameter is always 2r.

title: Constant-speed merry-go-round
subject: Physics
stem: A rider moves around a merry-go-round at constant speed. Is the rider's velocity constant? State the direction of the acceleration.
raw_stem: A rider moves around a merry-go-round at constant speed. Is the rider's velocity constant? State the direction of the acceleration.
correct: No. The speed is constant but the velocity direction changes continuously. The acceleration is centripetal: it points toward the centre.
formula: a_c = v² / R directed radially inward
steps: No. The speed is constant but the velocity direction changes continuously. The acceleration is centripetal: it points toward the centre.
trap: Constant speed does not imply constant velocity because velocity is a vector whose direction turns continuously.
teacher_check: In uniform circular motion, acceleration is strictly perpendicular to velocity, directed toward the center.

title: Distance versus displacement
subject: Physics
stem: When can the distance travelled equal the magnitude of displacement?
raw_stem: When can the distance travelled equal the magnitude of displacement?
correct: When the motion is along a straight line in one direction without reversal; then the path length equals the start-to-finish separation.
formula: |Δr| = Distance only when motion is rectilinear in one direction without turning back
steps: When the motion is along a straight line in one direction without reversal; then the path length equals the start-to-finish separation.
trap: Any change in direction makes distance strictly greater than displacement magnitude.
teacher_check: |Δr| <= Distance in all trajectories; equality holds only along a non-reversing straight path.

title: String breaks in circular motion
subject: Physics
stem: A stone moves in a horizontal circle on a string. If the string suddenly breaks, in what direction does the stone move immediately after release?
raw_stem: A stone moves in a horizontal circle on a string. If the string suddenly breaks, in what direction does the stone move immediately after release?
correct: It moves along the tangent to the circle at the release point, in the direction of its instantaneous velocity.
formula: v_tangential by Newton's First Law of Motion
steps: It moves along the tangent to the circle at the release point, in the direction of its instantaneous velocity.
trap: The stone does not fly radially outward; it flies tangentially in the direction of its instantaneous velocity.
teacher_check: Centrifugal outward flight is a fictitious frame artifact. In inertial frames, motion continues along the tangent line.

title: What keeps a planet turning?
subject: Physics
stem: What provides the centripetal force for a planet revolving around the Sun, and what is the direction of its acceleration?
raw_stem: What provides the centripetal force for a planet revolving around the Sun, and what is the direction of its acceleration?
correct: The Sun's gravitational force provides the centripetal force. The planet's acceleration points toward the Sun.
formula: F_grav = G M m / r² = m v² / r
steps: The Sun's gravitational force provides the centripetal force. The planet's acceleration points toward the Sun.
trap: No forward tangential force is needed to keep the planet in orbit; inertia maintains forward speed while gravity turns the velocity vector.
teacher_check: Centripetal acceleration is produced solely by the central gravitational force.

title: Horizontal throw versus drop
subject: Physics
stem: Two stones start simultaneously from the same height. One is dropped and the other is thrown horizontally. Neglect air resistance. Which reaches the ground first?
raw_stem: Two stones start simultaneously from the same height. One is dropped and the other is thrown horizontally. Neglect air resistance. Which reaches the ground first?
correct: They reach the ground at the same time because their vertical motions start with the same vertical velocity (zero) and have the same acceleration g.
formula: h = (1/2) g t² => t = sqrt(2h / g)
steps: They reach the ground at the same time because their vertical motions start with the same vertical velocity (zero) and have the same acceleration g.
trap: Horizontal velocity does not delay or hasten vertical free fall. Both vertical motions are identical.
teacher_check: Orthogonal motions are completely independent: vertical motion is governed exclusively by gravity.

title: Moon if Earth gravity vanished
subject: Physics
stem: Suppose Earth's gravitational pull on the Moon suddenly became zero and no other celestial body affected the Moon. What path would the Moon follow immediately afterward?
raw_stem: Suppose Earth's gravitational pull on the Moon suddenly became zero and no other celestial body affected the Moon. What path would the Moon follow immediately afterward?
correct: It would move in a straight line tangent to its former orbit with its instantaneous velocity.
formula: F_net = 0 => uniform rectilinear motion along tangent
steps: It would move in a straight line tangent to its former orbit with its instantaneous velocity.
trap: Removing force eliminates acceleration, not velocity. The Moon does not stop or drift randomly.
teacher_check: By Newton's First Law, when net external force is zero, the body continues along the instantaneous tangent line.

title: Why Earth does not fall into the Sun
subject: Physics
stem: The Sun attracts Earth gravitationally. Why does Earth not simply fall straight into the Sun?
raw_stem: The Sun attracts Earth gravitationally. Why does Earth not simply fall straight into the Sun?
correct: Earth has tangential velocity. Gravity continually bends that velocity toward the Sun, producing orbital motion rather than a straight radial fall.
formula: Curvature match: g_centripetal = v² / R bends straight line into closed orbit
steps: Earth has tangential velocity. Gravity continually bends that velocity toward the Sun, producing orbital motion rather than a straight radial fall.
trap: Gravity does not fail to pull Earth; Earth is in perpetual free fall toward the Sun but its forward tangential speed keeps it in orbit.
teacher_check: Orbital motion is continual free fall around the central body due to sufficient tangential velocity.

title: Coin tossed inside a train
subject: Physics
stem: A passenger tosses a coin vertically inside a moving train and the coin lands behind the passenger. What does that imply about the train's motion while the coin was airborne?
raw_stem: A passenger tosses a coin vertically inside a moving train and the coin lands behind the passenger. What does that imply about the train's motion while the coin was airborne?
correct: The train accelerated forward while the coin was airborne; after release, the coin did not share the train's continuing forward acceleration.
formula: Horizontal inertia: v_coin = v_train(t0); x_train(t) > x_coin(t) => lands behind
steps: The train accelerated forward while the coin was airborne; after release, the coin did not share the train's continuing forward acceleration.
trap: Do not treat the coin as being blown backward by air; the train accelerated forward under the airborne coin.
teacher_check: In an accelerating frame, an apparent pseudo-force acts backward, or from the ground frame the train accelerates past the coin.
